title: Ringed slice over an arbitrary sheaf: element-site presentation and exact extension by zero
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $A$ be a sheaf of sets in the chosen universe. Form the site $\mathcal C/A$ whose objects are pairs $(U,s)$ with $U\in\mathcal C$ and $s\in A(U)$, whose arrows $(V,t)\to(U,s)$ are arrows $v:V\to U$ with $A(v)(s)=t$, and whose covering families are those whose underlying families in $\mathcal C$ cover. This is a small site. There is a geometric equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/A)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/A$ taking $(F\xrightarrow p A)$ to $((U,s)\mapsto\{x\in F(U):p(x)=s\})$. Under this equivalence the ring $R_A=R\times A\to A$ corresponds to the sheaf $(U,s)\mapsto R(U)$. The localization geometric morphism $j_A:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/A\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ has module pullback $j_A^*:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_A)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] given by $(j_A^*M)(U,s)=M(U)$. This functor is exact and has an exact additive left adjoint $j_{A!}$. For an $R_A$-module sheaf $L$ on $\mathcal C/A$, $j_{A!}L$ is the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the presheaf $U\mapsto\bigoplus_{s\in A(U)}L(U,s)$; restriction along $v:V\to U$ sends the summand indexed by $s$ to that indexed by $A(v)(s)$ using the restriction of $L$. For any map of sheaves $B\to A$, applying this construction inside $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/A$ identifies its localization at $B\to A$ with $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/B$, with restricted ring $R_B$; the resulting restriction composed with $j_A^*$ is canonically $j_B^*$.

proof.text: The category of elements has objects $(U,s)$ with $U$ an object of $\mathcal C$ and $s\in A(U)$, and arrows $(V,t)\to(U,s)$ the arrows $v:V\to U$ satisfying $A(v)(s)=t$. Since $\mathcal C$ is small and every $A(U)$ is a set, the objects and arrows form sets. Declare a family covering exactly when its underlying family in $\mathcal C$ covers. Identities and composition preserve the displayed equality, and the identity, transitivity, and pullback axioms for coverings are inherited from the site axioms in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Thus $\mathcal C/A$ is a small site.

source.place: Tag 0791, lemma-localize-topos-site; site axioms from Tag 00VH

proof.text: For a sheaf $(F\xrightarrow p A)$, define its fibre presheaf on the element site by $F_A(U,s)=\{x\in F(U)\mid p_U(x)=s\}$. Restriction is well-defined because naturality of $p$ gives $p_V(x|_v)=A(v)(p_U(x))=A(v)(s)=t$ for an arrow $(V,t)\to(U,s)$, and the equalizer sheaf condition for $F$ restricts to the fibres, so $F_A$ is a sheaf. Conversely, for a sheaf $L$ on $\mathcal C/A$, take the presheaf of pairs $(s,x)$ with $s\in A(U)$ and $x\in L(U,s)$ and sheafify it; projection to $A$ is induced by $(s,x)\mapsto s$. On a covering, compatible pairs glue exactly when their first coordinates glue in $A$ and their second coordinates glue in the corresponding fibre, so the projection is a sheaf map. The map from $(F\to A)$ to the reconstructed sheaf sends $x$ to $(p(x),x)$, while the map back evaluates a pair at its fibre; both are inverse after sheafification by the sheaf condition. These maps are natural, giving the required equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/A)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/A$.

Let $p:\mathcal C/A\to\mathcal C$, $(U,s)\mapsto U$, be the projection. It is continuous: a covering of $\mathcal C/A$ maps to a covering of $\mathcal C$ by definition, and the fibre product $(U_i,s_i)\times_{(U,s)}(V,t)$ is $(U_i\times_UV,\,t|_{U_i\times_UV})$, so $p$ carries it to $U_i\times_UV$. It is cocontinuous: a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ of $p(U,s)=U$ is the image of the covering $\{(U_i,s|_{U_i})\to(U,s)\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction], restriction $L\mathcal G(U,s)=\mathcal G(U)$ is the inverse image of a morphism of topoi $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C/A)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$; under the fibre equivalence of the preceding step it is $\mathcal G\mapsto(\mathcal G\times A\to A)$, since the fibre of $\mathcal G\times A\to A$ over $s$ is $\{(x,s)\}\cong\mathcal G(U)$, and this is the localization morphism $j_A$. The product sheaf $R_A=R\times A\to A$ has fibre $R(U)$ at $(U,s)$, with the restrictions of $R$, so $R_A=j_A^{-1}R$; taking the structural ring map to be the identity gives a ringed-topos morphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Its module pullback $R_A\otimes_{j_A^{-1}R}j_A^{-1}M$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] is $j_A^{-1}M$, as tensoring over a ring with the ring itself is the identity; so $(j_A^*M)(U,s)=M(U)$ with the $R(U)$-action of $M$, a module sheaf in the sense of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $j_A^*$ is left adjoint to the module pushforward of that lemma.

source.place: Tag 04IE, lemma-localize-ringed-topos, clauses (1)-(2); continuity and cocontinuity of $j$ from sites.tex Tag 0791, lemma-localize-topos-site (verification omitted there, written here)

proof.text: For an $R_A$-module sheaf $L$ the presheaf $u_pL$ of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3) for $u=p$ is, at $U$, the colimit of $L(V,t)$ over the opposite of the category $I_U$ of triples $(V,t,\varphi:U\to V)$, an arrow $(V,t,\varphi)\to(V',t',\varphi')$ being an arrow $g:(V,t)\to(V',t')$ of $\mathcal C/A$ with $g\varphi=\varphi'$. The triples $(U,s,\mathrm{id}_U)$, $s\in A(U)$, form a discrete full subcategory $D_U$ (an arrow between two of them is $g$ with $g\circ\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}$). Every object $(V,t,\varphi)$ receives exactly one arrow from $D_U$, namely $\varphi:(U,A(\varphi)(t),\mathrm{id}_U)\to(V,t,\varphi)$, since such an arrow $g$ must satisfy $g=\varphi$ and then $s=A(\varphi)(t)$. Hence $D_U^{op}$ is final in $I_U^{op}$ and the colimit is $\bigoplus_{s\in A(U)}L(U,s)$, an $R(U)$-module since each $L(U,s)$ is an $R_A(U,s)=R(U)$-module; restriction along $v:V\to U$ sends the $s$-summand to the $A(v)(s)$-summand by $L$ of $v:(V,A(v)(s))\to(U,s)$, which is $R$-semilinear. Sheafifying this presheaf of modules using [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives $j_{A!}L$. An $R$-linear map from it to an $R$-module sheaf $M$ is, by the sheafification universal property, an $R$-linear presheaf map from the direct sum, i.e. a family of $R(U)$-linear maps $L(U,s)\to M(U)$ compatible with restrictions; this is exactly a morphism $L\to j_A^*M$. Thus $j_{A!}\dashv j_A^*$, naturally in $L$ and $M$, and $j_{A!}$ is additive.

source.place: Tags 04IE and 03CY; direct-sum calculation from the $u_p$ colimit in Tag 0791

proof.text: Kernels of module sheaves are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $(j_A^*M)(U,s)=M(U)$, so $j_A^*$ preserves kernels; it also preserves cokernels, being a left adjoint (preceding-but-one step, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]). Hence $j_A^*$ is exact. The functor $j_{A!}$ is a left adjoint (preceding step), so it preserves cokernels and is right exact; it remains to show that it preserves injections. Let $L_1\to L_2$ be injective; since kernels are sectionwise, each $L_1(U,s)\to L_2(U,s)$ is injective. Then the map of presheaves $\bigoplus_{s\in A(U)}L_1(U,s)\to\bigoplus_{s\in A(U)}L_2(U,s)$ is injective on every $U$, because a direct sum of injective maps of abelian groups is injective. The module sheafification of a presheaf has as underlying abelian sheaf the abelian sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and abelian sheafification preserves injections, being exact [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]; by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1) the forgetful functor to abelian sheaves is faithful and preserves kernels, so a map of module sheaves whose underlying abelian map is injective is injective. Hence $j_{A!}L_1\to j_{A!}L_2$ is injective, and $j_{A!}$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 04IE, clauses (2)-(4), and Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact (right exactness from the adjunction, injectivity from the sectionwise direct sum and exact sheafification)

proof.text: For a map of sheaves $B\to A$, an object of the iterated element site $((\mathcal C/A)/(B\to A))$ is an object $(U,s)$ together with $b\in B(U)$ mapping to $s$; sending it to $(U,b)$ gives a bijection on objects. An arrow over $(U,s)$ is an arrow $v:V\to U$ carrying $b$ to the section at $V$, so under this bijection it is precisely an arrow of the element site $\mathcal C/B$; the same observation identifies covering families. The restricted product ring $R\times A$ pulls back to $R\times B$, and the two restriction functors both evaluate a module at $(U,b)$ as $M(U)$. Therefore the localization over $B\to A$ is identified with $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)/B$, the composite restriction is canonically $j_B^*$, and repeating the objectwise identification for $C\to B\to A$ gives compatibility with further maps.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NA-7a3797386 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, all six steps, every cited statement, and Stacks sites.tex 0791 and sites-modules.tex 04IE (1)-(4), 04J4 and 03DJ. The statement matches the sources and is not weakened. Step 1 (the element site) is correct. In step 2 (the fibre equivalence) the presheaf of pairs is already a sheaf, so the extra sheafification is harmless. Step 6 (relocalization) is correct: s is determined by b, the coverings agree and the ring maps are identities. The three clause-restating helper nodes are gone, so the D1 return is repaired. I fixed three faults in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-proper-base-change/lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction.json. F1 (step 4): the u_p comma category had its arrows reversed, and A(f)(t) with f:V->U and t in A(V) is ill-typed. It now uses the triples (V,t,phi:U->V); the discrete part {(U,s,id)} is final, which gives the direct sum over s in A(U). F2 (step 5, E3): exactness of j_{A!} applied a direct sum to a short exact sequence of sheaves as if it were exact on each section, which is false because sheaf epimorphisms are only locally surjective. It now uses the 03DJ argument: right exact as a left adjoint, plus injectivity from injective maps on sections, exact sheafification (lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact) and the faithful forgetful functor that preserves kernels (lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful). F3 (steps 3 and 5): j_A existing as a morphism of topoi and j_A^* preserving cokernels had no support, and the step treated a definition as if it supplied the morphism. The repair shows that p is continuous and cocontinuous and cites lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction and lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction (structure map id, R_A tensor over R_A of M is M). So j_A^* is a left adjoint, and it is exact because kernels are computed on sections. Both added nodes are reviewed and in unit sk-thm-properbasechange. A DFS found no cycle through the item or its citer lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport. The module-colimits lemma is in sk-thm-reduction, which the unit cites, so it stays on the route and no tool_uses are needed.
